doc.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Plans, and his house in Algiers after Katrina
summary: He describes Algiers Point, evacuating to Florida, and returning to find his house under leaves but intact.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: What’s happening in the near future for you?

After this I have to get back because the CEO of my school — well obviously I’m from New Orleans so you know about the transition that we’re going through. I was fortunate I didn’t lose my house. I live in a section of town that was actually was settled before New Orleans, it’s called Algiers. Some people refer to it as Old Algiers and we call it Algiers Point. It’s across the river.

And as you know about the history of the music, there was a lot of jazz musicians who settled in Algiers who perform. I mean we have this walk of fame, in fact there’s a statue of Louis Armstrong right at Algiers Point. And it’s really interesting because you can take the ferry and cross the river and you can be right in the French Quarter from my house. And when I evacuated I stayed away for about two or three months in Florida, I was in Florida with my wife and my son and we went back three months later and — well actually I went back before then and I had to rake up like fifty bags of leaves. I’ll never forget it man, it was like I said there’s a house here somewhere. But no water.

Leaves. Like I had like leaves like I live under these oak trees I mean it’s a beautiful street it’s like this avenue. And it’s like these 300 year old oak trees. Some of them fell obviously from the wind breaking, but what happened was all of the wind just pushed all the leaves on my front porch. I’m telling you man, I had to like open the gate, move a tree branch, move the leaves out of the way, it was incredible, and open up my front door and I thought I was going to smell this wretched smell coming through my house but what happened was the electricity went out but it was turned back on so the refrigerator was still cold. It was just like one of these freak things. And maybe I had a couple of tiles off
